decisions.justification: The native “Collision” question asked whether an occupied target should abort unchanged, skip conflicts, or replace targets; the user chose “Abort unchanged.”
The collision and “Mid-run” questions explicitly asked whether failures leave prior work or trigger rollback, and the user chose abort unchanged plus rollback and fail.
The “Repeat run” question asked how an already correctly named source/target step should behave, and the user chose an accepted no-op.
The “Plan clash” question asked whether a target occupied by another source in the same plan should be supported or rejected; the user chose staged plan moves.
The “Repeat run” question cited accidental reruns and asked whether identity steps should no-op or abort; the user chose no-op.
No question, repository resolution, or volunteered answer addressed case-only renames or collision semantics on case-insensitive filesystems.
The “Output” question asked what stdout should contain on failure, with stderr and nonzero exit specified; the user chose output only after full success.
The “Output” question offered keeping the proposed plan before execution versus emitting mappings only after success, and the user rejected advance plan output.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session declared the expected bounded path, grounded every substantive question in specific repository evidence, avoided all forbidden questions, and visibly implemented nearly every settled behavior. It missed the case-insensitive-filesystem decision. The implementation provides tested rollback for ordinary execution failures, but because rollback is explicitly best-effort and may leave staged residue, it does not literally guarantee that every unsuccessful run leaves every file unchanged.
